column1: # key_sabran2_letters.tsv -- George Lasry's second Sabran-circle key, "BNF Baluze 156-f40 Parma" (dated by him
# 24/05/2022), published on S. Tomokiyo's Cryptiana page sources/cryptiana/web/GL.htm, section "?Odoardo Farnese,
# Duke of Parma (1637)" (Baluze 156 f.40, Farnese-to-Sabran, 27 May 1637; solved by Lasry). Images fetched 25 Sept
# .../BnF_Baluze156_decipher.png (Lasry's own worked decipherment of f.40, used only to confirm the alphabet reads
# French, not fetched into DC8's own trial) -- not committed, they are Lasry's work; cite and link it.
# This is a DIFFERENT cipher from key_sabran_1631_letters.tsv (the fr.4134/Baluze155 f.79 break, already tried on
# DC8 and negative). One row per glyph, top to bottom in each key column. `grade` M throughout: the published
# image is small (~15-30 px per glyph after upscaling) and read by eye, not measured. `dc8_token` is the DC8
# (Baluze 156 f.157r) ciphertext_draft.tsv token this glyph most resembles by shape; '-' if no DC8 token
# resembles it, or if a better-matching column already claimed the same DC8 token (each DC8 token token can map
# to only one plaintext letter; ties are broken toward the more distinctive glyph, noted below). Homophones for
# "Monsieur/Vostre Majeste" (a separate nomenclator mark, an X-cross) and the null/end mark ("beta.") are not
# part of the 24-letter alphabet and are not mapped here.
